title: Lipid panel (cholesterol)
what: A blood test from a vein that measures fats in your blood: total cholesterol, "bad" and "good" cholesterol, and triglycerides.
why: To check your risk of heart and blood vessel disease, if you have high blood pressure, diabetes, or extra weight, and to monitor treatment.
duration: the blood draw takes 3 to 5 minutes. Results usually take 1 to 2 days
tell_doctor: If you have diabetes or thyroid disease

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Strictly on an empty stomach: your last meal is a light dinner around 6 pm, and do not eat in the morning. You can drink water.

prepare.title: The day before
prepare.text: Ideally, avoid fatty food for 3 days before the test. No alcohol for one to two days.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own, especially cholesterol medicines.

steps: You sit down and rest your arm on the armrest
A band is tied on your arm, and the skin is cleaned with antiseptic
A quick prick, and blood fills the tube
The needle is removed, and a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes
Cholesterol targets differ for everyone. Your doctor sets yours

faq.a: "Bad" cholesterol, LDL, builds up in blood vessels. "Good" cholesterol, HDL, helps clear cholesterol away. The balance between them matters.

faq.q: How often should I check my cholesterol?
faq.a: Adults usually every few years, more often if you have risk factors. Your doctor will tell you how often.

reminders.text: Cholesterol test tomorrow. No fatty food at dinner, and do not eat after it. Water is fine.
